content.text: This section establishes the framework for developing and maintaining external partnerships that enhance student learning opportunities and prepare students for post-secondary success. Eduversal Partner Schools are committed to creating meaningful pathways that connect students with universities, employers, cultural institutions, and alumni networks, ensuring graduates are well-prepared for their chosen futures. The external partnerships and student pathways program supports the achievement of Schoolwide Learner Outcomes (SLOs), particularly Academic Excellence, Global Competence, Communication, and Innovation, while aligning with CIS Domain 9 (Community and Partnerships) and WASC Category C (Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth).
The following principles guide all external partnerships and pathway programs:

items: Student-Centered: All partnerships prioritize student benefit, learning outcomes, and future opportunities
Ethical Engagement: Partnerships maintain transparency, avoid conflicts of interest, and uphold school values
Equity and Access: All students, regardless of background or financial circumstances, have access to pathway support
EAL-Inclusive: Programs accommodate students whose first language is not English, providing appropriate support and resources
Data-Informed: Decisions are based on student outcomes, destination tracking, and partnership effectiveness data
Sustainable: Partnerships are built for long-term mutual benefit rather than short-term gains
content.title: 23.1.1 Guiding Principles

content.text: External partnerships encompass:

items: Higher Education Institutions: Indonesian and international universities, polytechnics, and vocational institutions
Industry and Business: Companies offering internships, work experience, and career insights
Professional Organizations: Bodies providing certifications, competitions, and professional development
Cultural Institutions: Museums, galleries, libraries, and cultural centers supporting educational programs
NGOs and Community Organizations: Partners supporting service learning, community engagement, and social impact
Alumni Network: Graduates contributing through mentorship, career guidance, and school support

content.title: 23.5.5 Alumni and Business Relationships
Safeguarding due diligence for mentors, hosts, and external instructors
items: Background check: every alumni mentor, work-experience supervisor, and external instructor who will have contact with students provides a current SKCK (police clearance) and two checkable references before any contact begins. Checks are renewed annually.
Written agreement: each external adult signs the school safeguarding agreement and completes a safeguarding briefing before their first session.
No unsupervised one-to-one contact, in person or in a private digital channel. Mentoring takes place in a school-monitored setting or on a school-monitored channel.

Monitored communication: all mentor-student communication runs through a school-approved channel with logs retained for the duration of the placement plus one year. Personal phone numbers, personal email, and personal social media are not used.
DSL sign-off: the Designated Safeguarding Lead approves every external placement and every mentor match before it starts, and keeps the register.
Concerns: any concern about an external adult is reported to the DSL immediately and handled under Section 9, including the allegations-against-adults procedure.
Work experience: placements additionally confirm the host employer's insurance cover, the student's working hours against Indonesian child-labour limits, and a named supervisor at the host site.

content.text: All formal external partnerships require appropriate approval: 23.7.2 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Template Formal partnerships are documented through MOUs containing: Essential MOU Elements:

steps: Parties: Full legal names of school (Yayasan) and partner organization
Purpose: Clear statement of partnership objectives
Scope: Specific activities and programs covered
Duration: Start date, end date, renewal provisions

Resources: Financial contributions, in-kind support, staffing
Intellectual Property: Ownership of materials created
Confidentiality: Data sharing and privacy requirements
Safeguarding: Child protection commitments
Liability: Insurance requirements, indemnification
Termination: Conditions for ending partnership
Dispute Resolution: Process for addressing disagreements
